title: Brake pad change: push two pads flush into their retainers each side of the disc, then swing the caliper down over them
instruction: Fit the new brake pads, then swing the caliper down over them.
context: A brake pad change, in the maker's order: with the caliper pivoted up out of the way on its upper guide pin, each new pad is pushed into the two sprung retainers on its side of the disc until its backing plate seats flush, the inner pad, with its shim and wear indicator, on the piston's side (the arms' left), the outer pad on the fingers' side (the arms' right); both go in from the front; then the 2 kg caliper is swung down about its pin so that its piston and its outer fingers pass either side of the 21 mm disc and the pads with 2 mm to spare, and its bridge closes over both pads' edges with 1 mm: a pad standing more than 1 mm proud stops the caliper short. Replacing brakes is a core task of automotive service technicians and mechanics (O*NET 49-3023: 'Repair, reline, replace, and adjust brakes'), and the pad change is the most common brake job. The corner is modelled at the scale of a small hatchback's front brake.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of the table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. A front brake corner of a small hatchback (Honda Jazz class) stands on a bench stand (a 40 x 40 mm post on a 220 x 160 mm foot plate, at (38, 10)), wheel off, turned so its caliper bracket faces the arms: a vented disc 262 mm across and 21 mm thick, its axis along y, centred at (38, 0) 25 cm up; the bracket at the disc's front edge carries four greased stainless pad retainers, two each side of the disc. The single-piston floating caliper (about 2 kg) hangs on its upper guide pin, pivoted up 100 degrees out of the way, its piston already pushed back; its lower guide bolt is out. Two new pads (131 x 55 x 15 mm with ears and steel backing plates, 0.2 kg each) stand on one ear, linings towards the disc's side they belong to, in a slotted wooden parts box (70 x 100 mm, 13 cm tall) on the table at (23, -13): the outer pad at y -11, the inner pad, with its shim and wear indicator, at y -15.
scoring: Photo, feeler gauge and inspection. 1.0, held for 2 s: both pads seated flush in their own retainers, the inner pad (shim and wear indicator) on the piston's side and the outer on the fingers' side, both linings facing the disc (pushed the full 12 mm in: a 1 mm feeler gauge does not enter between any ear and its retainer's end), the caliper swung down and shut over them (within 1 degree), and no gripper within 5 cm of the pads or the caliper's bridge. 0.3: both pads flush, without the 1.0 result. 0.1: one pad flush. 0 otherwise. A pad dropped off the bench caps the score at 0.1.
reset_notes: The pads back in their slots in the parts box, the caliper pivoted back up to 100 degrees on its pin. No seed changes the scene.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz on GPU. The caliper is a hinge on its upper guide pin, held where it is left by the pin's rubber sleeve, modelled as dry friction of 1.6 N m (above its weight's 1.4 N m). Pads slide into the retainers' channels with greased friction 0.3; the retainers' spring drag and snap are not modelled. Piston pre-pushed; brake hose, lower guide bolt and its torque left out. Caliper mass and retainer drag are estimates, not measured.
